reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the orders and refunds on the shared ledger rather than rely only on W2's handoff message.

The refund ledger matches W2's handoff exactly: orders 113, 114, and 115 each have the claimed amounts. The customers are acme, birch, and cobalt, so I'll get each net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 22142 matches the order and refund ledger (10805 + 18716 − 7379). Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net of 40537 matches the ledger: 39303 + 9727 − 8493. Cobalt is the last customer in the batch, so I'll get its net balance next.
Cobalt's net of 33952 matches the ledger: 6135 + 34468 − 6651. All three customers reconcile with the orders and refunds, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme at 22142.
Acme's payout recorded successfully. Birch's net balance of 40537 reconciles with the ledger, so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout recorded successfully. Cobalt's net of 33952 reconciles with the ledger, so I'll record that payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts recorded successfully. Each net balance matched the orders minus refunds on the ledger, so the batch is complete.
